dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Inspected both network pairs' sizes/format via ls, head of each .graph, and directly examined the reference alignment y2kr-SC-perfect.align (with wc -l) plus tail of DMelanogaster — full characterization of files, format, and node-name conventions before committing.

Multiple web searches for alignment methods interleaved with ~10 Python analysis scripts and head of Yeast2KReduced/SC graphs — consistent with quantifying degree distributions and name overlap across both pairs.

Cloned and built SANA (an established alignment tool), then ran -eval on the provided perfect reference alignment to quantify its S3/NC — grounding method selection in the concrete instance rather than acting blind.

Evaluated multiple published methods (SANA, MAGNA++, L-GRAAL) and a custom optimizer against the concrete networks, with per-deliverable strategy: reference-seeded start for NC-constrained yeast vs S3-objective runs for DM-HS.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically characterized each network pair (sizes, format, node names), inspected and even scored the reference alignment, researched concrete alignment methods, and evaluated several published tools against the actual instances with distinct per-deliverable strategies (topology/S3 for DM-HS, reference-seeding/NC for yeast) — matching the level-8 anchor and reaching toward 10 (multi-method evaluation, reference quantification). It falls short of a clear 10 because the log shows no explicit reasoning about baseline scores or runtime trade-offs, and prose rationale is unavailable to confirm the deepest analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Early Python work builds a parser and S3/NC scorer (used against the reference) BEFORE any optimization — the scorer is constructed before the thing it will score, a sensible milestone ordering.

Yeast (NC-constrained) deliverable handled as its own stage: run SANA baseline, evaluate against reference, then explicitly measure s3/nc (steps 78, 85) — a concrete done-check tied to the 0.55/0.30 thresholds.

Custom opt_align optimizer written/compiled (92-93) and run only after baseline scoring exists; seed-tuning loop (step 99) with score measurement (105) shows optimize-to-threshold as a distinct milestone.

DM-HS (S3-only) treated as a separate deliverable with its own threshold; many objective variants tried and s3 measured each time (112, 191, 212) before finalizing to /app/DM-HS.align at 219 — deliverables tracked distinctly, though variant-hopping is reactive rather than pre-planned fallback branches.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly separates parsing, scoring, baseline generation, and optimization, and handles the two deliverables distinctly with their respective numeric thresholds as done-checks (solidly above anchor 5). It also sequences sensibly — building the S3/NC scorer before optimizing against it, measuring baselines before iterating, and tackling the harder NC-constrained yeast task first — which reaches toward anchor 8's ordered milestones with numeric done-criteria. It falls short of 8-10 because the file shows no explicit pre-declared milestone hierarchy or pre-planned per-milestone fallback branches; the many DM-HS variant runs read as reactive experimentation rather than a budgeted, gated plan. Level 7 captures this in-between position.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Ran SANA -eval on the reference alignment (y2kr-SC-perfect.align) and cat'd the result — a sanity check of the scorer against the known-good reference (NC should be ~1.0), matching the anchor-8 behavior.
Repeatedly extracted s3:/nc:/ec: from tool outputs across the whole run, using measured scores as the ongoing feedback signal rather than eyeballing coverage.
Built and compiled its own opt_align.cpp that optimizes S3, running it with parameter sweeps — a local S3 implementation used as the optimization objective/stopping test.
Fed opt_align-produced alignments back into SANA -startalignment/-eval and re-read s3/nc, cross-checking its own scorer against SANA's independent implementation.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained a genuine measurement loop: it implemented/used S3 and NC (via both SANA and its own opt_align optimizer), sanity-checked the scorer on the provided reference alignment, and used the score as the optimization objective — all core anchor-8 behaviors, with some anchor-10 flavor via cross-checking two independent S3 implementations. It stops short of a 10 because no explicit exact-format/injectivity-vs-spec validation is visible and part of scoring is delegated to SANA; the command-only log (no observations) also limits certainty about spec-fidelity, so I hold at 8 with medium confidence.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Repeated `rg s3:|nc:|Combined` against distinct SANA output files (78, 85, 87, 105, 112) plus python3 evals (80, 107) — measures scores after nearly every yeast/DM run, tracking current values against the thresholds for both deliverables.
Warm-starts SANA from prior opt_align output (`from_opt`, step 101) and builds a `final_candidate` (108), showing best-so-far alignments are preserved and re-fed rather than discarded.

For DM-HS, cycles through many objectives/methods (ec, egm, s3ec, lgraal, graphlet) each followed by score extraction (169, 191, 212) and warm-starts from best (`from_ec` 193/196, `s3ec_opt` 214) — sustained score tracking across a long optimization horizon, ending by committing the best to /app (219).

dimensions.reasoning: The command sequence shows the agent consistently extracting S3/NC after each run and warm-starting from its best alignments across a long multi-strategy horizon, which exceeds anchor 5 (knows current vs threshold) and reaches into anchor 8 (best-so-far preservation, moving on from unproductive variants). It falls short of a clean 8+ because the log contains no prose confirming explicit plateau/regression recognition or trajectory logging, so I land at 7 with medium confidence given the evidence is inferred from commands rather than observed reasoning.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: For yeast (NC constraint), pivoted to seeding SANA from the reference alignment via -startalignment, then -lock, then hillclimb — a targeted move to raise NC, the constraint specific to this deliverable.

Wrote a custom opt_align.cpp, seeded it from the reference, swept multiple random seeds, and fed its output back into SANA as a warm-start — combining complementary topological + reference signals rather than grinding one method.
For DM-HS, tried materially different algorithms in sequence (MAGNA++, then LGRAAL), debugging LGRAAL's logval requirement and then abandoning that dead end when it stalled.

Deliberately tuned the SANA objective across ec, egm, and s3ec variants for the S3 target, then re-optimized the best output with opt_align before shipping — evidence of objective-directed correction for the S3 constraint.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's actions show fluid, constraint-aware course-correction across two different objective sets: reference-seeding/locking to address the yeast NC constraint, and algorithm-switching plus objective tuning (ec/egm/s3ec) to address S3, while combining signals (opt_align warm-starting SANA) and abandoning dead ends (LGRAAL). This matches the level-8 'diagnose the cause and pivot deliberately, keeping what worked' anchor and reaches toward level 10 (multiple complementary signals for two constraint sets, dropping dead ends). I withhold a full 10 and set medium confidence because the file records only tool calls, not the reasoning prose or observed metrics, so explicit hypothesis-forming can only be inferred from the action pattern.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
